question:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed acyclic graph with |E| > 0. Which of the following must be true?
I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge.
II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs: I. Since G is a directed acyclic graph (DAG), there must be at least one vertex with no incoming edges. In other words, there must be a vertex that children can come from, but none come to. So this statement is true. II. Since G has |E| > 0, there must be at least one vertex from which all other vertices come, and therefore there must be at least one vertex with an outgoing edge. So this statement is also true. III. There is no requirement that there must be a vertex with neither an incoming nor an outgoing edge, even though there must be someone coming to all other vertices, there doesn't have to be someone that nobody is coming to. So this statement is false. The correct answer is (C). I and II only.

question: Given image \begin{tabular}{|llll|} \hline 7 & 1 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 7 & 6 \\ 6 & 6 & 5 & 7 \\ \hline \end{tabular} , and the bit-depth of the image is 4. Suppose you want to use the thresholding technique to segment the image. What is the appropriate threshold value based on the histogram of the image? Follow the following rule when you do thresholding or grouping: pixel $(i, j) \in$ Group A pixels if $g(i, j) \leq$ current threshold $\mathrm{T}$; pixel $(i, j) \in$ Group B pixels otherwise, where $g(i, j)$ is the intensity value of pixel $(i, j)$.
model_outputs: To find the appropriate threshold value for thresholding, we first need to determine which intensity value plays the role of a "middle" intensity, which can effectively separate the pixels into two groups: lighter (Group A) and darker (Group B). Let's look at the given histogram (image) and find the middle intensity. \begin{tabular}{|llll|} \hline 7 & 1 & 6 & 0 \\ 3 & 3 & 7 & 6 \\ 6 & 6 & 5 & 7 \\ \hline \end{tabular} The sum of all intensity values is 7 + 1 + 6 + 0 + 3 + 3 + 7 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 5 + 7 = 46. The middle intensity value can then be found by dividing the sum by 9 (the total number of pixels). In this case, 46/9 without any rounding would give approximately 5.11. The intensity value closest to 5.11 is 5 (intensity value "F" in the histograms). So, the appropriate threshold value for recording the middle intensity is "F". The answer is (F).
